frontmatter.title: Foundations of Data Science for Everyone

children.value: In every facet of life, making effective decisions requires data. To understand and make use of data, you must thoroughly understand it.

One of the first stages of a data science project is Data Exploration. The basic way to explore a dataset is to look at the raw data in a table, but this approach --- while important --- is unlikely to reveal anything interesting. We must

the data: understand how each of our variables may be related to one another. You can do this visually with a scatter plot, or you can calculate Pearson’s Correlation coefficient: a number that represents how related to variables are.
Python is the programming language of choice for data scientists, and as a result there already exists robust tools for data analysis. The first one we will look at is
Making decisions requires data. To use data, you must understand it.

Frequentist vs Bayesian interpretation of probability

children.label: Frequentist vs Bayesian interpretation of probability

children.value: Frequentist: “The fraction of times something happens is the probability of it happening.”

children.html: P(E)=frequency of event, E(After 11 coin flips) P(coin = heads)=611=0.55(After 101 coin flips) P(coin = heads)=51101=0.504\begin{align*} P(E) &= \textrm{frequency of event, E} \\ \textrm{(After 11 coin flips) }P(\textrm{coin = heads}) &= \frac{6}{11} = 0.55 \\ \textrm{(After 101 coin flips) }P(\textrm{coin = heads}) &= \frac{51}{101} = 0.504 \\ \end{align*}P(E)(After 11 coin flips) P(coin = heads)(After 101 coin flips) P(coin = heads)​=frequency of event, E=116​=0.55=10151​=0.504​

children.value: belief about whether the coin is fair (50/50 of getting heads/tail) or not.”
The Bayesian statistician could get 10 heads in a row, but if they have a prior belief that the coin is fair, then they will still expect to get 50% heads and 50% tails in the long run.
